checked_obligation: Verify that the proof establishes that the sequence f_n(x)=x^n on [0,1] does not converge uniformly.
reason: For every x in [0,1), x^n tends to 0, while f_n(1)=1, so the stated pointwise limit f is correct. If f_n converged uniformly to g, then it would converge pointwise to g, hence g=f by uniqueness. With epsilon 1/2, uniform convergence would require strict inequality |f_n(x)-f(x)|<1/2 for all n>=N and x in [0,1]. Choosing x=2^{-1/N} gives x in [0,1), f(x)=0, and |f_N(x)-f(x)|=x^N=1/2, contradicting that requirement. The listed group-theoretic rules are irrelevant and are not used.
